identity.title: POCUS gallbladder: stones, wall thickening, sonographic Murphy sign

technique.how: Curvilinear probe, subcostal or intercostal RUQ window, patient supine then left lateral decubitus with deep inspiration. Image the gallbladder in long and short axis: look for echogenic, shadowing, mobile stones; measure anterior wall (>3 mm abnormal); look for pericholecystic fluid; test sonographic Murphy sign (maximal tenderness with probe over the gallbladder). Trace the common bile duct.
technique.prerequisites: Fasting improves distension; adequate window may need lateral decubitus; operator credentialed in RUQ POCUS.
technique.contraindications: None; do not delay resuscitation of an unstable patient to scan.

interpretation.positive_finding: Stones with wall thickening, pericholecystic fluid or a sonographic Murphy sign indicate acute cholecystitis (ED POCUS sens 0.87, spec 0.82); stones alone with typical pain support biliary colic.
interpretation.negative_finding: No stones, normal wall and negative sonographic Murphy sign make calculous cholecystitis unlikely (LR- 0.16) but do not exclude acalculous cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis or cholangitis.
interpretation.pitfalls: Contracted post-prandial gallbladder, duodenal gas, polyps and sludge mimic or hide stones; wall thickening is non-specific (ascites, hepatitis, heart failure, hypoalbuminaemia). Analgesia blunts the sonographic Murphy sign.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive for cholecystitis: surgical consultation, antibiotics, consider admission; stones only: outpatient follow-up if pain resolves; negative with low pretest probability: pursue alternatives.

estimates.population: Symptomatic ED patients scanned by emergency physicians; 8 prospective studies, n=710
estimates.reference_standard: Radiology ultrasound, CT, MRI or surgical findings
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.898/(1-0.880) = 7.48; LR- = (1-0.898)/0.880 = 0.12; from pooled sensitivity 89.8% and specificity 88.0%
estimates.quote: pooled estimates for sensitivity and specificity were 89.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 86.4% to 92.5%) and 88.0% (95% CI = 83.7% to 91.4%), respectively.

estimates.population: ED patients with suspected cholecystitis, academic centre, convenience sample n=189 scanned by 43 EM residents/attendings (median 2 scans each)
estimates.quote: bedside ultrasonography were sensitivity 87% (95% confidence interval [CI] 66% to 97%), specificity 82% (95% CI 74% to 88%), positive likelihood ratio 4.7

sources.citation: Ross M, Brown M, McLaughlin K, et al. Emergency physician-performed ultrasound to diagnose cholelithiasis: a systematic review. Acad Emerg Med. 2011;18(3):227-235.
Summers SM, Scruggs W, Menchine MD, et al. A prospective evaluation of emergency department bedside ultrasonography for the detection of acute cholecystitis. Ann Emerg Med. 2010;56(2):114-122.
Trowbridge RL, Rutkowski NK, Shojania KG. Does this patient have acute cholecystitis? JAMA. 2003;289(1):80-86.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a negative POCUS to exclude acalculous cholecystitis in critically ill/ICU patients or cholangitis when jaundice or sepsis is present.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Gallbladder findings with fever, jaundice, hypotension or dilated CBD suggest cholangitis or gangrenous cholecystitis: urgent antibiotics, surgical and biliary (ERCP) consultation.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Accuracy reported for EM residents and attendings after brief training; the sonographic Murphy sign and wall measurement are the most operator-dependent elements.
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency physician credentialed in RUQ POCUS (typical ACEP-level training, ~25 supervised scans); pooled data are from EP operators, not sonographers.

extraction_notes: Ross 2011 pooled estimate is for cholelithiasis, not cholecystitis; LRs computed by extractor from the pooled sens/spec (no pooled LR in abstract). Summers 2010 gives EP-performed POCUS for acute cholecystitis with a wide sensitivity CI (23 pathology-confirmed cases). Trowbridge 2003 RCE cited as index for the clinical context; its sonographic Murphy data are not visible. Component-level accuracy (wall thickness, sonographic Murphy alone) not entered because no reachable source reports it with a location.
